Neutrino Urca emissivities using the CompOSE PT(GRDF2-DD2) equation of state

Reference composition, microscopic self-energies, Dirac and Landau masses, and a five-prescription comparison at 10⁸ and 10⁹ K. This report documents what was implemented, tested, and left unresolved. The full reproducible source and reduced inputs are included in the companion ZIP.

2Lepton channels (e, μ)

1. Main Urca comparison

All models use the actual cold beta-equilibrated composition from CompOSE and EOS-derived effective masses. The Friman–Maxwell, both Bottaro, and Shternin curves represent neutron-branch modified Urca; the Alford curve is an adapted finite-width charged-current rate, not its complete published finite-temperature implementation.

2. EOS composition and microscopic masses

The cold table provides n, p, e and μ fractions. The general-purpose CompOSE table supplies vector and scalar fields Vn, Sn, Vp, Sp (IDs 10051, 10052, 11051, 11052). For a momentum-independent RMF self-energy, mD_i = m_i − S_i and mL_i = sqrt(pF_i² + mD_i²).

Finite-temperature data distinction: the general-purpose table begins at 0.1 MeV (1.16×10⁹ K). The fields at 10⁸ K are extrapolated from the two lowest slices in T². Their agreement with the independent cold composition is a validation of small thermal sensitivity, not a demonstration of exact T² dependence.

3. Comparison of the five prescriptions

ReferenceNuclear interactionPropagatorImplemented hereMain limitation
Friman–Maxwell (1979)OPE; historical αₙ and βₙ factorsFixed virtual denominatorsNSCool neutron-MU expression; legacy muon extensionHistorical reference only; no threshold enhancement
Bottaro et al. (2024)OPE + magnetic ρ + phenomenological Landau; βₙ=0.68Constant ~1/μℓTriangular Eqs. (3.28–3.29) and full angular integral Eq. (3.34)Neutron branch with constant virtual denominators
Shternin et al. (2018)In-medium model informs 0.6 R_A+0.2 R_B enhancementMomentum dependent, zero widthPublished approximate neutron-branch enhancementCoefficients not recalibrated to DD2 interaction; fails at DU threshold
Alford et al. (2024), adaptedPhenomenological nucleon spectral widthBreit–Wigner mass convolutionDegenerate DU kernel × BW-allowed triangle probabilityNot full finite-T polarization/vertex calculation; adapted only

Common EOS input

Cold 1D baryon/lepton fractions are interpolated with PCHIP. The general-purpose microscopic fields are interpolated as bicubic splines in log density and charge fraction. Independent beta-equilibrium roots are used for cross-checks. EOS composition remains cold in the emissivity calculations.

Numerical formulas and parameters

Friman–Maxwell uses the historical coefficient 8.55×10²¹ with αₙ=1.76−0.63(1.68/kFn)² and βₙ=0.68. Bottaro uses the triangular neutron-branch formula with ρ strength Cρ=1.4, mπ=139.57 MeV, mρ=769 MeV, and historical phenomenological Landau couplings. Shternin uses 0.6 R_A + 0.2 R_B, with the momentum-dependent propagator factors evaluated analytically. The adapted Alford calculation uses Breit–Wigner Dirac-mass widths Wn=Wp=T²/(5 MeV) and a leading degenerate direct Urca kernel. Complete equations, constants and code functions are in docs/METHODS.md and calculations/compare_compose_four.py.

All units, thresholds, and whether electron+muon or a single channel is included are preserved in the CSV column names.

No direct Urca threshold crossing occurs between 0.16 and 0.98 fm⁻³ in this CompOSE cold composition. Consequently the model comparison here cannot validate the NWA’s finite-width behavior at threshold.

Not yet established: independent reproduction of Bottaro Fig. 6, full microscopic Shternin interaction, conserving in-medium weak vertex corrections, proper spectral widths from the same EOS, independent near-threshold crossover, and production-level neutrino cooling validation.

5. Starting a GitHub working repository

The ZIP uses a runnable calculations/ directory containing the scripts, their compact inputs and generated outputs. Primary scripts are deliberately retained rather than silently refactored, to preserve the published numerical baseline. Future refactoring should be done with regression checks.

python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
python calculations/test_final.py
python calculations/test_T8_reference.py
python -m unittest discover -s tests -v

# Reproduce the complete figures and CSV outputs
python calculations/build_final.py
python calculations/run_dd2_T8_reference.py

git init
git add .
git commit -m "Initial CompOSE DD2 Urca comparison"

Suggested scientific milestones: (1) full finite-T Alford response; (2) independent reproduction of Bottaro Fig. 6; (3) consistent Shternin nuclear vertices; (4) an EOS with an accessible DU threshold; (5) conserving widths and weak vertex corrections; (6) proton branch and pairing. See docs/ROADMAP.md.

Source and provenance

CompOSE cold EOS #302 and general-purpose EOS #301. Full source archives are not included in the repository; file hashes are recorded in docs/input_archive_manifest.json. References: Bottaro et al. (2024), Shternin et al. (2018), Friman & Maxwell (1979), Alford, Haber & Zhang (2024). The last two references are described in docs/REFERENCES.md.
